message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius roughly 2½–3 times that of Jupiter (about 20,000 km). Its mass is still uncertain—some estimates put it at around 15–20 Jupiter masses, which would make it borderline between a massive planet and a low‑mass brown dwarf—but in terms of sheer size, it’s the biggest object we’ve found in another solar system.
